portal_hypertension.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is a rising cause of chronic liver disease. Liver stiffness measurement (LSM) to assess disease stage is gaining popularity but can demonstrate heterogeneous results in clinical practice. Moreover, portal hypertension may develop early in MASLD in the absence of cirrhosis. These observations may be partially explained by features not assessed in the current NASH-CRN liver biopsy staging, including features of porto-sinusoidal vascular disorder (PSVD).
